positive_text: A pseudo-random generator for elliptic curves can be constructed by selecting a random point $ P \in E(\mathbb{F}_p) $ and iteratively computing $ P_i = [k]P $ for random scalars $ k $.

Let $E(\mathbb{F}_q)$ be an elliptic curve group and $G$ a generator. If Alice computes $A = aG$ and Bob computes $B = bG$, then $aB = bA$ defines a shared secret known only to both parties.

anchor_text: The multivariate approximation error in a tensor grid follows a product rule under independent smoothness conditions in each coordinate.
positive_text: For a tensor product quadrature rule, the error decays as the product of the convergence rates in each dimension.

negatives.text: The Lebesgue constant measures the sensitivity of the interpolant to perturbations in the function values.

Multivariate Gaussian quadrature rules constructed from tensor products of one-dimensional rules preserve optimality for multivariate polynomials.

anchor_text: A Hölder continuous solution to a parabolic equation is guaranteed when the kernel of the associated evolution operator is Hölder in time.
positive_text: The expected pathwise Hölder continuity of a process is implied by the uniform Hölder estimates on the transition density of the underlying generator.

negatives.text: A cylindrical Wiener process in an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space leads to a Feynman–Kac-type formula when integrated over linear functionals of the process.

The Markov transition operator of a diffusion can be expressed as an integral over the space of continuous paths weighted by the corresponding stochastic measure.

anchor_text: Any bounded operator $ A $ can be uniquely written as $ A = U |A| $ where $ U $ is a partial isometry and $ |A| $ is the square root of $ A^*A $.
positive_text: Every complex observable $ A $ can be represented uniquely as $ A = U \sqrt{A^* A} $, where $ U $ is an isometric transformation.

anchor_text: A volume form $ \varepsilon $ is modular if it satisfies $ \mathcal{L}_\xi \varepsilon = 0 $ for all $ \xi \in \mathfrak{g} $, the Lie algebra of the group acting on the manifold.
positive_text: A modular volume form is a top-degree form invariant under a group action with a non-vanishing differential Jacobi determinant.

anchor_text: A subshift is self-factorizable if it admits a factor map from itself which is injective on a positive-measure subset.

anchor_text: The probability of decoding error for a code of rate $ R $ decreases exponentially with block length at a rate given by the error exponent $ E(R) $.

anchor_text: Let $ f $ be a contraction mapping on a complete metric space. For any $ \varepsilon > 0 $, there exists $ n $ such that $ d(f^n(x), f^{n+1}(x)) < \varepsilon $, implying convergence to a fixed point.

anchor_text: If a term is well-typed and closed, it is either in normal form or reducible by some beta-reduction.

anchor_text: When a source has memory, its entropy rate is lower than its symbol entropy; this reduction can be exploited for more efficient encoding over multiple symbols.

anchor_text: For a shift-invariant compact topological system $ (X, \sigma) $, the topological past tail $ \sigma $-algebra $ \mathcal{F}_- $ is trivial in the sense that the only clopen sets in $ \mathcal{F}_- $ are those with empty or full interiors.

anchor_text: The probability of the intersection $T^{-n}(A) \cap B$ tends to $\mu(A) \mu(B)$ as $n \to \infty$ for all $A, B$.

anchor_text: If $f'(x) \not\equiv 0 \mod p$, then a root of the equation $f(x) = 0$ in $\mathbb{F}_p$ can be uniquely extended to a root in $\mathbb{Z}_p$ via Newton iteration.

anchor_text: If $ f_n \to f $ uniformly on $ [a, b] $, then $ \lim_{n \to \infty} \int_a^b f_n(x) \, dx = \int_a^b f(x) \, dx $.

anchor_text: The subgroup $ \mathrm{Gal}(L/K) $ is normal in $ \mathrm{Gal}(L/F) $ if and only if $ K $ is a normal extension of $ F $.

positive_text: The rank of the Alexander–Conway homology of a knot is at least $ 2^{\text{braid index}} $.

The HOMFLY polynomial of a knot has degree in $ z $ bounded by the braid index minus one.

anchor_text: Elliptic curve signatures can be recovered from a message and a signature point using the public key and the hash.
positive_text: Digital signatures can be recovered from a message and a signature element using the public key and the digest.

negatives.text: The private key is a randomly chosen integer used to generate a public element via exponentiation in a cyclic group.

An element $ g $ in a group $ G $ is a generator if every element of $ G $ can be expressed as $ g^k $ for some integer $ k $.

anchor_text: The topological entropy $ h_{\text{top}}(X) $ is the exponential growth rate of the number of words of length $ n $ in $ X $.
positive_text: The topological entropy $ h_{\text{top}}(T) $ is the exponential growth rate of the number of $ (n, \epsilon) $-separated sets.

negatives.text: A transformation $ T $ is conservative if for every set $ A $ of positive measure, the return times to $ A $ are unbounded almost surely.
A joining of the systems $(X,\mu,T)$ and $(Y,\nu,S)$ is a measure $\lambda$ on $X \times Y$ with marginals $\mu$ and $\nu$ such that $(T \times S)^*\lambda = \lambda$.
A point $x \in X$ is recurrent under $T$ if there exists an increasing sequence $n_k \to \infty$ such that $T^{n_k}x \to x$ as $k \to \infty$.

anchor_text: Each partial configuration can be completed to an optimal configuration without removing any initially included element.
positive_text: Any independent set $ A $ can be augmented to form a basis without excluding any specific subset from $ A $.

negatives.text: A set $ A $ in a matroid is closed if and only if no element can be added to it without violating independence.

anchor_text: A theory extending an effectively decidable one is conservative if all theorems it proves are also provable in the base theory.
positive_text: A computable extension of a decidable set is conservative if all recursive functions it defines are already representable in the base set.

negatives.text: A recursive structure is effectively consistent if its valid sequences are recursively enumerable.

anchor_text: Two parties can agree on a shared secret by exchanging scalar multiples of a public base point on an elliptic curve.
positive_text: Two parties can securely agree on a shared secret by exchanging exponentiated values in a cyclic group using a public generator.

negatives.text: The number of usable key values in a public-key cryptosystem depends on the size of the cryptographic group $ G $, with the best security achieved when the group has a large prime order.

A blind signature construction must deform the internal scalars with random values so that an observer cannot determine the private key involved in the signing process.

anchor_text: Every derivation in a constructive logic can be represented as a sequence of inductively defined proof steps.
positive_text: The inductive nature of an intuitionistic proof guarantees that each inference corresponds to a valid step in a recursive construction.

negatives.text: An equivalence $ \phi \leftrightarrow \psi $ is intuitionistically valid only if both implications are valid.

anchor_text: If $ f $ is differentiable at $ x_0 $ and has a local maximum at $ x_0 $, then $ f'(x_0) = 0 $.
positive_text: If $ f $ has a local maximum at $ x_0 $ and is differentiable there, then for all infinitesimal $ h $, $ \frac{f(x_0 + h) - f(x_0)}{h} $ has standard part zero.

negatives.text: If $ f $ is piecewise smooth at a point $ x $, the internal hyperfinite Fourier series evaluated at $ x + \varepsilon $ and $ x - \varepsilon $ yields values infinitesimally close to the average of the left and right nearstandard limits.

If $ ^\ast f_n \to ^\ast f $ with the standard part converging pointwise and with infinitesimal variation, then the integral of $ f $ coincides with the standard part of the integral of $ ^\ast f_n $ for $ n $ infinite.
A function $ f $ is continuous at $ x_0 $ if for every hyperreal $ x $ infinitely close to $ x_0 $, the standard part of $ f(x) $ equals $ f(x_0) $.

anchor_text: A lattice is modular if the modular law holds for all elements $a, b, c$ with $a \leq c$.
positive_text: A poset is modular if for all elements $a, b, c$ with $a \leq c$, $a \vee (b \wedge c) = (a \vee b) \wedge c$.

anchor_text: In quantum mechanics, the possible sets of outcomes of yes/no measurements correspond to a complete lattice of orthogonal subspaces of the Hilbert space.
positive_text: The set of all closed subspaces of a Hilbert space $ \mathcal{H} $ forms a complete lattice under inclusion.

anchor_text: A knot is fibered if its complement fiber over the circle with monodromy determined by a braid respecting a pseudo-Anosov mapping class.
positive_text: A braid closure is fibered if the braid induces a monodromy that acts pseudo-Anosov on the punctured disk.

anchor_text: The determinant of a quadratic form $ Q: V \to \mathbb{Q} $ over a number field $ K $ with ring of integers $ \mathcal{O} $ is the square of the volume of the fundamental domain of the associated module $ \mathcal{O}^n $ scaled by a lattice embedding.
positive_text: The determinant of a lattice $ L \subseteq \mathbb{Q}^n $ is the square of the covolume of the lattice when embedded in the ambient rational space under the induced inner product.
